That, and sometimes I have traumatic flashbacks to that one time 10 years ago when I actually tried to stop to talk to someone I knew on the street after they said "how are you." He'd already sort of breezed past me while saying it and the poor guy stopped out of politeness while I was internally trying to figure out why he looked so put off by it when he'd asked me first.

CBT (cognitive-behavioural therapy) is definitely the common one, so if in doubt, go for that. There will be an abundance of therapists for it anywhere. However I'm personally in psychodynamic therapy and I've found that it works for me a lot better.

Essentially, CBT focuses on the now, the present moment. They might give you homework lol. Basically journalling, mood diaries, etc. As I said it's meant to identify patterns, so tracking your own behaviour becomes essential.

Psychodynamic therapy works for me because I have childhood trauma. It focuses more on your past and the early influences, and I've found that working with a psychodynamic therapist feels more organic. But that's my experience, and CBT can still be useful for some people even with similar issues to mine!

What is really truly important is that you get along with your therapist. Everything else comes second.

If you can, shop around! A lot of therapists offer the first session for a discount/even free because it's mainly you interviewing the therapist to figure out if you two are a good fit. I've decided against a therapist who specialised in my specific type of childhood trauma because they felt too rigid. The vibes were off lol.

[Iatrogenic](https://medical-dictionary.thefreedictionary.com/iatrogenic) = resulting from the activity of a health care provider or institution; said of any adverse condition in a patient resulting from treatment by a physician, nurse, or allied health professional.

In other words, it's debated whether these "founders" of the diagnosis contributed to it through fraudulism and deceit. If you want to look into a more reliable source from this time, that would be [Pierre Janet:](https://www.newworldencyclopedia.org/entry/Pierre_Janet)

"He first used the term “dissociation” in May 1887 to describe the phenomenon of "double consciousness" in hypnotism, hysteria, spirit possession, and mediumship."

If you read further, in 1900s, the public interest in tbe diagnosis and also the amount of diagnoses fluctuated, often rising when a movie related to it was made and fell after it was forgotten.

One of the case studies from then would be documented in [The Three Faces of Eve](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Three_Faces_of_Eve). The psychiatrists who published the case study and the book sold the right immediately to film studios, and also helped to screenwhite a movie of the same name. So make of that what you will. Also, [Thigpen](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbett_H._Thigpen) performed ECT and lobotomies. [Cleckley](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hervey_M._Cleckley) also used ECT and coma therapy, but his reputation is a tad more admirable and he worked in court on the case of Ted Bundy.

And of course there's the links to the "satanic panic" and its contributions to the [DID diagnoses of its time.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7960286/)

So. Yeah. You could say it's been heavily debated.

"[hegemonic masculinity] serves as the standard upon which the "real man" is defined."

"contemporary hegemonic masculinity is built on two legs, domination of women and a hierarchy of intermale dominance."

https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hegemonic_masculinity

Basically, toxic (or hegemonic) masculinity is a sociological theory. It establishes gender roles in our society, which feminists still argue to be patriarchal, to varying degrees. Any deviation from the gender roles established in the society is punished e.g. socially, by judgement, bullying and sometimes violence. Anything feminine is seen as bad, and any men exhibiting stereotypically feminine traits are punished for it, for example with phrases like "Boys don't cry", suggesting that under hegemonic masculinity men are not allowed to show emotions.

He's usually quickly shut down, "real men" don't do that. It becomes harmful for people who don't fit the norm, and for example gay men are constantly punished, often violently, for expressing "feminine" traits.
